name: Lethal Congenital Contracture Syndrome Type 1

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for LCCS1

criteria.description: Severe fetal akinesia with multiple joint contractures detected prenatally
Congenital arthrogryposis multiplex congenita involving limbs
Hypoplastic or absent anterior horn cells in spinal cord on histopathology
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the GLE1 gene
Neonatal respiratory insufficiency leading to early death

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe prenatal contractures and arthrogryposis with confirmation by genetic testing for GLE1 mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often confirmed postmortem due to lethality in utero or shortly after birth.

occasional.symptomName: Abnormal form of the vertebral bodies

laboratory: Normal routine laboratory tests; no specific biochemical markers
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing multiple joint contractures and reduced fetal movements
Postnatal skeletal radiographs showing arthrogryposis and scoliosis
MRI may show hypoplasia of anterior horn cells
other: Histopathology of spinal cord showing absence or severe hypoplasia of anterior horn motor neurons

distinguishingFeatures: Different genetic cause (e.g., mutations in ERBB3)
Presence of additional central nervous system malformations
Variable severity and survival beyond neonatal period
Lack of characteristic anterior horn cell hypoplasia

redFlags: Severe fetal akinesia with multiple joint contractures detected prenatally
Neonatal respiratory failure refractory to intervention
Absence of anterior horn cells on spinal cord histology
references: Lahtinen AM, et al. Lethal congenital contracture syndrome type 1 is caused by a mutation in the GLE1 gene. Am J Hum Genet. 2008.
Orphanet: Lethal congenital contracture syndrome type 1. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases.
Hall JG. Arthrogryposis multiplex congenita: etiology, genetics, classification, diagnostic approach, and general aspects. J Pediatr Orthop B. 1997.
